transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (Citrine), Priya (Citrine), Liam (Citrine)

Auto-summary: Quick scrub of this week's benchmark results; focus on traffic-pattern tuning — short tails and cold-starts; decide if dedicated slot needed; agree next steps to run head-to-head workload with longer sequences.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for carving time today, quick check-in, goal is to triage the latency tail on the mid-sprint runs and talk routing/playbook decisions. Maya is going to walk through the bench notes.
[00:18] Maya: yep, thanks. so high level we re-ran the sprint-3 harness against your sample trace from last week, the difference we saw: average token latency for Redwood on the 256-seq subset is ~42ms vs incumbent ~60ms, p95 is 210ms Redwood vs 330ms incumbent, p99 420ms vs 680ms. those are aggregated across mixed batch sizes 1-8.
[00:43] Priya: wait did you include cold-starts? we saw a bunch of cold-start spikes on our environment that pushed p99 higher.
[00:50] Maya: good call. our reported numbers include a 5% cold-start sample since your trace had intermittent warmups. if we strip cold-starts, p99 comes down to ~340ms. but tail shape is sensitive to the traffic bursts you saw on Tuesday.
[01:10] Evan: curious about throughput under burst, our QPS drops when we get 80 concurrent streams—what did Redwood observe?
[01:18] Maya: under a synthetic ramp to 80 concurrent streams with the current config (4-bit quant, continuous batching, KV prefix cache enabled) we observed sustained throughput of ~260 requests/min for the 512-seq profile, throughput dropped 15% when we disabled prefix cache.
[01:34] Liam: is that requests/min or tokens/sec? need to align units.
[01:38] Maya: sorry requests/min. in tokens/sec that's roughly 8k tokens/sec aggregate at that load given your avg seq length.
[01:45] Priya: sounds reasonable. the incumbent reports similar aggregate tokens/sec but the tails are worse which we suspect is due to cache eviction pattern.
[01:54] Jordan: quick note — we instrumented the KV cache eviction boundaries; when sequence length distribution shifts (more long sequences) the eviction churn increases and we see tail latency bumps.
[02:05] Evan: so what can we tune short-term to flatten the tail?
[02:08] Maya: three levers right now: 1) set a short-lived prefix cache TTL for conversational prefixes (reduces cold KV misses), 2) tweak continuous-batching policy to cap max batch delay at 8ms for high-latency sensitive routes, 3) route long-seq requests to a quantized larger-model variant with higher memory so it avoids eviction.
[02:30] Priya: for the route suggestion, is that an automated smart-route or a static route?
[02:34] Maya: we can do policy-based smart routing — rules based on seq length and latency SLO. it can fallback to the smaller model if capacity constrained.
[02:42] Liam: we worry about correctness/regression when changing model variant. any A/B or shadow testing support?
[02:48] Maya: yes, rollout supports canary, A/B, and shadow. we recommend canary with 10% traffic and eval hooks for prompt set QA.
[02:57] Evan: the big blocker for us is compliance — if we move to dedicated slot we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
[03:05] Jordan: understood. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS, audit log forwarding to your SIEM, and private VPC peering. we'll attach SOC2 docs but Maya will include dedicated security appendix.
[03:17] Priya: can you share the raw traces and the latency-by-config spreadsheet? we want to correlate with our app logs.
[03:22] Maya: yes will upload both to the shared drive, I'll include p95/p99 breakdowns per route and per batch size. link will be in the follow-up.

[03:35] --- deep dive on a specific anomalous run (timestamp 2026-03-17 02:12 UTC) ---
[03:37] Maya: on that run we saw a pattern: short bursts of 30msec followed by tail spikes at ~700ms correlated with a pattern of 40% longer sequences entering the pool causing eviction churn. sample trace attached in notes.
[03:52] Evan: that aligns with our Friday incident when a marketing campaign sent long-form queries. could routing rules have diverted those to a different pool?
[03:59] Maya: not in the test config — everything hits same pool. we can create a dedicated long-seq pool, or enable auto-scaling with burst slots. caveat: auto-scaling adds a cold-start window for new slots.
[04:15] Priya: what's the measured cold-start penalty? we saw 1.2s on first request historically.
[04:20] Maya: correct ballpark — cold-start depends on quantization warm-up; for 4-bit quant it's usually 900–1300ms when a new GPU instance is spun up, but warm reuse eliminates that after first few requests.
[04:32] Jordan: if cold-start is a concern, dedicated reserved slots avoid spin-up, or we can keep a small pool warm with warm-standby capacity. Jordan: the pricing delta is in the spreadsheet I'll send.

[04:45] Evan: okay so tactical plan?
[04:47] Maya: tactical: 1) enable prefix TTL of 5 minutes for conversational routes, 2) cap batching delay at 8ms for latency-SLO routes, 3) create a long-seq routing rule to a warm pool for peak hours. we'll run a 24hr test with your Friday spike replay.
[05:05] Priya: how do we replay exact spikes? we will dump the trace and you run the harness?
[05:10] Maya: yes please upload the 5k-request trace; we'll run it through our local harness and Redwood lab concurrently to compare. we will also run the incumbents harness to get head-to-head.

[05:20] Liam: one more thing about metrics — can you include token-level cost deltas? we need to know unit economics impact of dedicated vs hosted.
[05:27] Jordan: will include token-level cost and projected monthly burn at current QPS. also include cost with warm-standby.

[05:34] --- brief Q&A on eval hooks ---
[05:36] Maya: eval hooks can run your prompt set on canary returns and compute regression metrics; we can gate rollout on those.
[05:42] Evan: great.

[05:45] --- recap and decisions ---
[05:46] Jordan: recap: Redwood will send latency-by-config spreadsheet, raw traces, and security appendix for dedicated slots by Wednesday. Maya will produce p95/p99 tail chart and set up the long-seq routing rule in the lab test. Citrine will provide the Friday spike trace and run head-to-head baseline tests. we'll reconvene next Tuesday for results review or earlier if any blocker.
[06:10] Priya: thanks everyone.
[06:12] Liam: thanks.
[06:14] Jordan: thanks, end call.
